ai.description: The Malabar Fungoid Frog (Ranidae) reaches 5–8 cm. It is reddish-brown with a distinct pale cream or yellow lateral fold and dark spots. Its skin is smooth with a rounded, blunt snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Malabar Fungoid Frog is best identified by the distinct, fleshy-white or cream-colored glandular fold running along its upper flanks, which contrasts sharply with its dark, reddish-brown body.
ai.habitat: The Malabar Fungoid Frog inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, as well as plantations, across the Western Ghats at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Malabar Fungoid Frog is primarily nocturnal and often hunts for insects on the forest floor, frequently congregating near water bodies during the monsoon season.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Malabar Fungoid Frog is an explosive breeder that spawns in temporary rain pools during the monsoon season (June–August), laying large clutches of gelatinous eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Malabar Fungoid Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, occurring across states from Maharashtra to Kerala at elevations up to 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Malabar Fungoid Frog produces a series of rapid, low-pitched "chuck-chuck" notes, typically heard calling from the leaf litter near forest streams during the monsoon.
